questions.text: Why initialize alpha to zero in the residual y = x + tanh(alpha) * cross_attention(x, visual)?

options.A: To make every visual token receive an equal attention weight.
options.B: To make the new visual branch contribute zero at initialization.
options.C: To prevent the visual branch from ever learning during training.
options.D: To replace the text representation with the visual representation.

questions.explanation: Because tanh(0)=0, the added visual contribution is zero and the residual output equals x at initialization.

questions.text: An image produces 196 patches and another produces 900. A Perceiver resampler uses K=64 latents per image. How many output tokens does each image produce?

options.A: 196 for the first image and 900 for the second.
options.B: 64 for the first image and 900 for the second.
options.C: 196 for the first image and 64 for the second.
options.D: 64 for each image, independent of its patch count.

questions.explanation: The learned latent count K sets the output token count per image regardless of how many patches attend as keys and values.

questions.text: What does interleaved_mask(["intro", "IMG0", "a", "IMG1", "b"]) return, with columns ordered IMG0, IMG1?
questions.explanation: Intro has no preceding image; a sees IMG0; b sees only its most recent preceding image, IMG1.
